edition.notes: The text preserves Carolingian orthography, folio marks in square brackets, and the e-caudata, which an optical text layer commonly renders as a caret or a question mark. A comparison must treat those as orthography and not as readings.

edition.title: The Gregorian Sacramentary under Charles the Great, edited from three MSS. of the ninth century by H. A. Wilson

passages.context: The Hadrianum carries the three orations of the 1962 Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost as its mass for the TWELFTH Sunday after Pentecost: the collect with habundantiam pietatis (Wilson's apparatus recording that Ottobonianus 313 already reads abundantia, the 1962 ablative) and adicias (the 1962 contracted spelling); the super oblata Respice domine with fragilitati (the apparatus recording fragilitatis in O, the 1962 genitive); and the ad complendum Sentiamus domine quaesumus as in 1962. The Gregorian series runs one Sunday ahead of the 1962 numbering through this stretch: its Dominica X is Pateant aures (1962 Pentecost IX) and its Dominica XI is Deus qui omnipotentiam tuam (1962 Pentecost X). The Ottobonianus margin cues copied in Wilson's footnotes attach the 1962 Pentecost-XI chant set - Ant. Deus in loco sancto suo, Resp. In deo sperauit cor, Off. Exaltabo te domine, Com. Honora dominum - at the foot of Wilson p. 171, one opening before this mass, while the footnote against Dominica XII itself cues Respice domine in testamentum and Panem de caelo, the 1962 Pentecost-XIII chants. The exact remote artifact bytes were re-fetched and their SHA-256 matched this record before reading.

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The papal sacramentary sent by Hadrian I to Charlemagne, transmitted with the supplement long ascribed to Alcuin. It is the immediate ancestor of the medieval and Tridentine Roman Mass books and the second great reservoir the twentieth-century reform drew its orations from.
work.title: Sacramentarium Gregorianum (Hadrianum)
